Profile likelihood for a ctsem julia fit

Source: R/ctFitProfile.R
ctFitProfile.Rd

Fixes one raw parameter at a sequence of values, re-optimising all the others at each, and reports how the likelihood changes. This shows whether the data determine the parameter, and gives likelihood based intervals. The curvature at the estimate can mislead about this along a flat direction (see Directions with no curvature in ctFitUncertainty).

Usage

ctFitProfile(
  fit,
  parameters = NULL,
  points = 8L,
  step = NULL,
  growth = 1.6,
  level = 0.95,
  maxiter = 500L,
  verbose = 0,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L)
)

Arguments

fit

a ctJuliaFit.

parameters

which parameters to profile: raw parameter names, indices, NULL for all of them, or "flagged" for only those the fit's own diagnostics question (parameters at the edge of their transform, unidentified directions, and intervals wider than the curvature supports). Profiling every parameter of a large model takes many optimisations.

points

maximum points per side.

step

first displacement, in raw units. NULL takes half of each parameter's standard error where the fit has one, so an identified parameter gets several points inside its interval, and 0.5 otherwise.

growth

factor the step is multiplied by after a point that changed the likelihood by less than the target, so a flat direction is walked out quickly.

level

confidence level setting the likelihood-ratio bar.

maxiter

iteration cap for each constrained optimisation.

verbose

0 for silence, 1 to report each point as it is computed.

cores

The most CPU cores the profile uses at once. By default the two sides of each parameter's profile run one after another in this session, on that many engine threads. When the fit itself took more than five minutes to optimise, they run up to cores at a time instead, each in a background R session with its own Julia session. This needs the future package. The sessions stay open for the next call, and ctJuliaKill('workers') ends them. The profile is the same either way, except that with several sessions every side finishes before $better is reported.

Value

An object of class ctFitProfile, with print and plot methods. $profile has one row per point (parameter, raw value, transformed value where there is one, log likelihood, and drop from the estimate). $summary has one row per parameter (verdict, limits, and how far each side was walked). $better is NULL unless a constrained fit beat the estimate, in which case it holds that point and the run stopped there.

Details

Each point is a constrained optimisation, so a profile can find that the fit was not at a maximum. When that happens the run stops and the better point is returned in $better. Refit from there and profile again.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Needs a working julia backend, so the example is inert where Julia is
# absent -- including on CRAN, whose check machines have none.
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
  model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
    LAMBDA = matrix(1))
  model$pars$indvarying <- FALSE
  fit <- ctFit(ctsemtestdat, model, backend = 'julia', cores = 1)

  # Two named parameters; parameters = "flagged" profiles only those the
  # fit's own diagnostics doubt, and NULL profiles every one.
  result <- ctFitProfile(fit, parameters = c('drift_eta1', 'mm_Y1'))
  print(result)
  plot(result)
  # Julia keeps running between calls, holding what it has compiled;
  # this ends it.
  ctJuliaKill("session")
}
# }
